# Stop AI coding agents installing hallucinated packages

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-agent-hallucinated-packages/


**Check that a package exists on the registry before an AI agent installs it. Code models invent plausible package names, and attackers can register those names. [ExactGround](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground)'s free hook blocks installs of names that do not exist in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor, and its hosted API answers the stricter question: does this function exist in the exact version you use?**

*Facts on this page were checked against the linked sources and ExactGround v0.1.5 on October 3, 2026.*

## How often agents invent packages

- In the USENIX Security 2025 study by Spracklen et al., 16 models generated 576,000 code samples. Of the 2.23 million packages they referenced, 440,445 (19.7%) did not exist, and there were 205,474 unique invented names ([paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity25/presentation/spracklen)).
- The rate was at least 5.2% for commercial models and 21.7% for open-source models.
- The names repeat. The authors re-ran 500 prompts that had produced a hallucination, 10 times each. In 43% of those cases the same invented name came back in all 10 runs, which is what makes registering it with malware (*slopsquatting*) practical.
- Trend Micro's follow-up dataset of 100 agent web-development tasks found that "neither approach fully eliminates the threat" ([trendmicro/slopsquatting](https://github.com/trendmicro/slopsquatting)). It compared reasoning agents with "vibe coding" plus MCP validation.

A rule in `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` saying "never invent packages" is text the model may ignore. A hook is code that runs on every install.

## Exists is not the same as safe

There are four separate questions, and a registry lookup answers only the first:

| Question | Who answers it |
|---|---|
| 1. Does the name exist on npm or PyPI? | ExactGround hook (free) and `check_packages` |
| 2. Is it the package you meant, from the expected owner, and not a fresh look-alike? | ExactGround flags young, rarely downloaded look-alikes of popular names and npm security placeholders. Ownership and provenance need your own review or a supply-chain scanner. |
| 3. Was this exact version published? | ExactGround hook and `check_packages` |
| 4. Does the function or method the agent calls exist in that version? | ExactGround API `check_symbols` / `check_diff` |

A package that exists can still be malicious, or a legitimate package can be compromised. ExactGround does not scan package contents. Pair it with a malware or supply-chain scanner and your lockfile.

## Try it in one line

```console
$ npx -y github:alidaram99/exactground#v0.1.5 check pypi:requests pypi:reqeusts react@99.0.0
OK      pypi:requests
BLOCK   pypi:reqeusts — "reqeusts" does not exist on PyPI; did you mean "requests"? (it is 1 edit away)
BLOCK   react@99.0.0 — version 99.0.0 of "react" was never published (latest is 19.3.0)
```

## Install it in your agent

- **Claude Code:** `claude plugin marketplace add alidaram99/exactground`, then `claude plugin install exactground@exactground-marketplace`.
- **Codex:** `codex plugin marketplace add alidaram99/exactground --ref v0.1.5`, then trust the hook in `/hooks`.
- **Gemini CLI and Cursor:** `exactground init gemini --write` or `exactground init cursor --write` in your project.

What the hook covers:
- `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, `bun`, `npx`, `pip`, `uv`, `poetry` and `pdm` install commands it can parse.
- Bare installs such as `npm install`, `uv sync` and `poetry install`, checked against the lockfile, so a dependency the agent wrote into `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` is caught too.
- Private packages: list them in `.exactground.json` and approve that file with `exactground trust` in a terminal. The hook ignores a policy file that no human approved.

Commands it cannot check are denied, not waved through. That covers installs inside `node -e`, `python -c`, `$(...)` and `eval`, program names built at run time (such as `& ('np'+'m')`), and loops or installs whose program or package name is a variable. A loop with a literal `npm`, `npx` or `pip` in its body is checked like any other command. If the registry or the checker fails, the hook denies too.

**Out of scope, on purpose.** ExactGround is a cooperative guardrail, not a sandbox. It stops an agent that hallucinates or mistypes a name in a normal install command. An agent running as your user that deliberately obfuscates its commands can defeat any hook-based guard, including this one. Examples include writing its own scripts, or building names and paths at run time in ways no rule anticipates. For an agent you treat as adversarial, use an OS sandbox or container, or a separate OS user ([SECURITY.md](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground/blob/main/SECURITY.md)).

## Check that an API exists in your exact version

Many hallucinations are real packages used wrongly. `useActionState` does not exist in React 18, and `numpy.asfarray` was removed in NumPy 2.0. The hosted ExactGround API answers these questions from the published package itself:
- npm: `.d.ts` declarations, read with the TypeScript compiler.
- Python: wheels, parsed statically and never executed.

The API has been live on the Apify Store since October 3, 2026. Calls need your Apify API token.

It is an MCP server billed per check:
- `check_symbols`: $0.002 per symbol.
- `check_packages`: $0.0005 per package.
- `check_diff`: $0.01 per diff.

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http exactground https://dropin-apis--exactground-api.apify.actor/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN"
```

## FAQ

### What is slopsquatting?

Slopsquatting means registering a package name that AI models tend to invent, so that agents and developers who trust the suggestion install the attacker's code.

### Does a package existing on npm or PyPI mean it is safe?

No. Existence rules out invented names and versions that were never published. Whether the package is the one you meant, who owns it, and what its code does are separate checks.

### Can ExactGround stop an agent that is trying to get around it?

Not reliably, and it does not claim to. It is built for agents that make mistakes, not agents that evade. Contain adversarial agents with an OS sandbox, a container or a separate user.

## Related

- Up: [all guides on this site](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/)
- Next: [stop agents claiming "done" without evidence](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-coding-agent-done-without-evidence/) (DoneLatch)
- **[Install ExactGround (free, MIT)](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground)** · [hosted API on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/exactground-api)

# Stop AI coding agents claiming "done" without evidence

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-coding-agent-done-without-evidence/


**A coding agent's "done" is only evidence when the checks you chose ran after its last change and their results are tied to that exact state of the code. [DoneLatch](https://github.com/alidaram99/donelatch), a free MIT tool for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor, refuses acceptance until such fresh passing checks exist and a deliberate fault shows the check can actually fail.**

*Facts on this page were checked against the sources linked inline and the DoneLatch v0.1.2 README on October 3, 2026.*

## Why "the agent said it passed" is not enough

- In Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey, 66% of developers who answered the AI-frustrations question picked "AI solutions that are almost right, but not quite", the most-cited answer; 45.2% picked "debugging AI-generated code is more time-consuming" ([survey](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai#ai-tool-frustrations)). These are survey answers, not a measured failure rate.
- A Claude Code bug report describes the model calling work "verified green" and done without running the project's canonical build-and-test command ([anthropics/claude-code#63861](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/63861), May 30, 2026).
- A Codex report describes background tasks whose final message says a command ran, while the host shows no observable command record or real exit code ([openai/codex#34152](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/34152), July 19, 2026).

Two different gaps show up here. The agent may not have run the check at all. Or it ran a check that cannot fail for the bug you care about.

## The three things to require

| Requirement | What it rules out | How DoneLatch does it |
|---|---|---|
| **Fresh:** the checks ran after the last relevant change | "Tests passed" from before the final edit | Each receipt binds the Git HEAD, watched file names, SHA-256 content hashes, modes and the config hash. Any later change makes it stale. |
| **Recorded:** results come from the tool, not the agent's summary | A narrative of success with no command behind it | `run` executes the approved commands itself and writes a signed receipt with their results and output |
| **Sensitive:** the check can detect a representative fault | A green test that would also pass with the feature broken | `faultcheck` injects a fault you define into a temporary copy and requires the check to fail with your declared marker and exit code |

The third row is a small negative control, the idea behind mutation testing. DoneLatch's demo shows why it matters. A persistence test that only checks `saveSettings() === true` still passes when the write is deleted, so DoneLatch refuses "done". A check that reads the saved bytes catches the same fault, and DoneLatch accepts.

## Set it up (about a minute, Node.js 24+)

```sh
npx --yes github:alidaram99/donelatch#v0.1.2 init        # writes receipts.yml (does not run anything)
# Edit receipts.yml: one trusted acceptance command and one meaningful fault.
npx --yes github:alidaram99/donelatch#v0.1.2 trust       # HUMAN ONLY: review and type APPROVE <hash>
npx --yes github:alidaram99/donelatch#v0.1.2 run
npx --yes github:alidaram99/donelatch#v0.1.2 faultcheck
npx --yes github:alidaram99/donelatch#v0.1.2 verify-done # exit 0 only for current, sensitive evidence
```

Then attach it to the agent's stop event, so the agent cannot finish its turn on stale or missing evidence:

| Agent | Hook event | Install |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `Stop` | `claude plugin marketplace add alidaram99/donelatch`, then `claude plugin install donelatch@donelatch-marketplace` |
| Codex | `Stop` | `codex plugin marketplace add alidaram99/donelatch --ref v0.1.2`, then install it and trust the hook in `/hooks` |
| Gemini CLI | `AfterAgent` | `gemini extensions install https://github.com/alidaram99/donelatch --ref v0.1.2` |
| Cursor | `stop` | manual adapter in the [agent install guide](https://github.com/alidaram99/donelatch/blob/main/docs/AGENT-INSTALL.md) |

When evidence is missing or stale, the hook asks the agent for one correction turn. After that it reports the work as UNVERIFIED instead of looping.

## Limits

- **Humans approve the checks.** `trust` runs only in an interactive terminal and records the hash of the exact configuration outside the repository. Changing `receipts.yml` requires a new approval.
- **The approval does not cover everything.** It does not pin the contents of the scripts your checks call, `PATH` resolution or the inherited environment.
- **You choose the fault.** DoneLatch does not invent a correctness oracle. A check passes this gate only for the fault you wrote down.
- **It is a cooperative guardrail.** Hooks can be disabled, skipped or time out, and then they fail open. A same-user agent that deliberately obfuscates or rewrites local files can defeat any hook-based guard, including this one. That class is out of scope. For an adversarial agent, use an OS sandbox, a container or a separate OS user. Enforce acceptance with `verify-done` in a CI step the agent cannot edit.
- **Local signatures are not independent attestation.** The same OS user can read the signing key.

## FAQ

### How do I make Claude Code run the tests before it says it is done?

Add a `Stop` hook that runs a verifier and blocks the stop when evidence is missing. DoneLatch's Claude Code plugin does this. It requires a passing `run` and `faultcheck` for the current files before `verify-done` accepts.

### Is a passing test suite enough evidence?

Not on its own. The tests must have run after the last change, and at least one of them must fail when the behavior you care about is broken. A check that cannot fail is not evidence.

### Does this replace code review or mutation testing?

No. It is a small, explicit completion gate for agent workflows. Full mutation testing, independent review and production monitoring still have their place.

### Can a determined agent get around it?

Yes, if it runs as your user and sets out to evade the check. Treat the hook as a guardrail for cooperative agents. Use OS-level isolation and a CI acceptance step for agents you do not trust.

## Related

- Up: [all guides on this site](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/)
- Next: [stop agents installing packages that do not exist](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-agent-hallucinated-packages/) (ExactGround)
- **[Get DoneLatch (free, MIT)](https://github.com/alidaram99/donelatch)** · [website](https://alidaram99.github.io/donelatch/)

# Why App Store Review Counts Differ by Country

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/app-store-reviews-differ-by-country/


**Apple's App Store doesn't have one global pool of reviews — ratings and reviews belong to the country storefront where they were left**, so querying only `us` and expecting "all" of an app's reviews will always undercount it. There's no single endpoint that returns a worldwide total: a defensible collection has to query every storefront you actually care about and record which one each review came from.

## Why this happens

Apple's own [ratings-and-reviews help page](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/monitor-ratings-and-reviews/view-ratings-and-reviews/) states plainly that reviews and ratings vary by App Store country or region — a user in Germany reviews the `de` storefront, a user in Japan reviews the `jp` storefront, and those pools don't merge anywhere Apple exposes publicly. An app with 2 million US ratings can simultaneously have a few hundred in a smaller market, and both numbers are real, scoped totals — not a partial view of one true number.

This Actor's `countries` input makes that explicit rather than hiding it: each app is fetched **once per country you list**, and every review and app-details row carries its own `country` field, so you can tell at a glance which storefront a number came from instead of assuming it's global.

```json
{
  "type": "app",
  "appId": "570060128",
  "country": "gb",
  "name": "Duolingo: Language Lessons",
  "averageRating": 4.72,
  "ratingCount": 5480861,
  "version": "7.142.0"
}
```

Run the same `appId` with `"countries": ["us"]` and you'll get a different `ratingCount` on the matching `app`-type row for `us` — both are correct, for their own storefront.

## What "get all App Store reviews" actually means

There's no API parameter, on this Actor or Apple's own endpoints, that returns a true cross-country total — because that total doesn't exist as a single number anywhere in Apple's systems; the App Store itself only ever shows country-scoped ratings to users. The practical approach:

1. Pick every storefront that matters for your use case (your top markets, or every country you ship in).
2. Pass them all in `countries`, e.g. `["us", "gb", "de", "au", "jp"]`.
3. Treat each `app`-type row's `ratingCount`/`averageRating` as that country's number, and sum review **rows** (not ratings) across countries yourself if you need a combined review count.

## Pagination and rate-limit boundary

Within one country, Apple's own public feed caps out at **500 reviews per app** (10 pages of 50) — a separate, additional limit on top of the per-country scoping above, confirmed against the live feed, not assumed. Older unauthenticated review-feed access has also been reported throttled under heavy unauthenticated load; this Actor's retry-and-fallback behavior (JSON feed first, XML feed second) exists partly because of that real-world flakiness, not just for robustness on paper.

## Limits

Up to 500 reviews per app **per country** — add more countries for more coverage, not a higher per-country cap (there isn't one to ask for). No developer-response text in any country's feed. A rating count you see here can differ from what a dashboard shows if that dashboard is already summing countries differently, or looking at a different moment in time.

## Pricing

Pay per event — **$0.0002 per row** ($0.20 per 1,000), no subscription. Querying 5 countries for one app costs the same per-row rate as 1 country; you simply get up to 5× the rows.

**[Open App Store Reviews Scraper on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)**

## FAQ

### Is there a way to get a true worldwide App Store review total?

No — Apple doesn't expose one, on this Actor or anywhere else publicly, because ratings and reviews are stored and shown per storefront. The closest equivalent is summing review rows across every country storefront you query yourself.

### Why did my review count drop between two runs?

It's unlikely review counts actually dropped; more likely a different set of `countries` was passed, or Apple's feed paginated slightly differently between requests. Compare the exact `countries` list and `maxReviewsPerApp` used in both runs before assuming data loss.

### How many countries should I query?

As many as are relevant to your use case. For competitor monitoring, your top 3–5 markets by install base usually capture most of the signal; for completeness, the App Store is distributed across [175 countries and regions](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/), though most apps have meaningful review volume in only a fraction of them.

### Does `sinceDate` work per country or globally?

Per country, within each app × country pairing being fetched — the Actor stops paging for that specific app/country combination once it reaches a review older than `sinceDate`, independently of how other countries for the same app are progressing.

### Where do I actually run this?

See the [App Store Reviews Scraper](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/app-store-reviews-scraper/) page for inputs, output shapes and code samples, or the [competitor-reviews guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/competitor-app-store-reviews-no-connect-key/) if you're specifically monitoring an app you don't own.

# App Store Reviews Scraper: any app, no Connect key

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/app-store-reviews-scraper/


The **App Store Connect API** only gives you reviews for apps your team owns, and it needs a private key. To read what users say about **any** app, including competitors, in any storefront, this Actor collects reviews from Apple's public customer-review feed and adds the app's public metadata. It needs no login and no Connect key.

## What you get

**One row per review:**

| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| `appId`, `appName`, `country` | `570060128`, `Duolingo: Language Lessons`, `us` |
| `reviewId`, `title`, `text`, `rating` (1–5) | `14612250135`, `Fun`, `Very fun and…`, `5` |
| `version`, `date`, `userName` | `7.142.0`, `2026-09-30T13:01:34-07:00`, `…` |
| `voteCount`, `voteSum` | helpfulness votes |

**Optionally, one app-details row per app × country:** name, developer, price and currency, average rating, rating count, version, release dates, genres, content rating, size, minimum OS and description.

App-details row from a real run:

```json
{
  "type": "app",
  "appId": "570060128",
  "country": "us",
  "name": "Duolingo: Language Lessons",
  "developer": "Duolingo, Inc",
  "price": 0,
  "currency": "USD",
  "averageRating": 4.72302,
  "ratingCount": 5481026,
  "version": "7.142.0",
  "currentVersionReleaseDate": "2026-09-28T17:42:01Z",
  "genres": ["Education", "Social Networking"],
  "contentRating": "4+",
  "url": "https://apps.apple.com/us/app/duolingo-language-lessons/id570060128?uo=4"
}
```

## Use cases

- **ASO and product feedback:** pull every recent review of your app into a spreadsheet or database and track ratings by version.
- **Competitor monitoring:** watch a competitor's rating, review volume and release cadence across countries.
- **Market research:** compare what users complain about across the top apps in a category and storefront.

## Run it in the Apify Console (no code)

1. Open the **[App Store Reviews Scraper](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)** and click **Try for free**.
2. Paste App Store URLs or numeric app ids, for example `https://apps.apple.com/us/app/duolingo-language-lessons/id570060128` or `570060128`.
3. Choose countries (`us`, `gb`, `de`…), the maximum number of reviews per app, and optionally a `sinceDate`.
4. Click **Start**, then export the dataset as CSV, Excel or JSON.

## Run it from code

Replace `<owner>/app-store-reviews` with the Actor id shown on its Store page.

### Node.js (`apify-client`)

```js
import { ApifyClient } from 'apify-client';

const client = new ApifyClient({ token: process.env.APIFY_TOKEN });

const run = await client.actor('<owner>/app-store-reviews').call({
  apps: ['570060128'], countries: ['us'], maxReviewsPerApp: 50, includeAppDetails: true,
});
const { items } = await client.dataset(run.defaultDatasetId).listItems();
for (const row of items) console.log(row.type, row.type === 'app' ? `${row.name} ★${row.averageRating}` : `${row.rating}★ ${row.title}`);
```

### Python (`apify-client` ≥ 3)

```python
import os
from apify_client import ApifyClient

client = ApifyClient(os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"])
run = client.actor("<owner>/app-store-reviews").call(
    run_input={"apps": ["570060128"], "countries": ["us", "gb"], "maxReviewsPerApp": 200},
)
for item in client.dataset(run.default_dataset_id).list_items().items:
    print(item["type"], item.get("rating"), item.get("title"))
```

### curl (one call, results in the response)

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/<owner>~app-store-reviews/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"apps":["570060128"],"countries":["us"],"maxReviewsPerApp":50}'
```

## Limits

- **Up to 500 reviews per app per country.** Apple's public feed stops there (10 pages × 50). To get more coverage, add more `countries`, since reviews differ by storefront.
- Developer replies are not part of Apple's public feed, so `developerResponse` is always `null`.
- Reviews come newest first. `sinceDate` stops paging once older reviews are reached.

## Pricing

**$0.20 per 1,000 rows** ($0.0002 per review or app-details row), pay per event. You pay only for rows delivered, with no subscription.

**[Open the App Store Reviews Scraper on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)**

# Azure Content Moderator retirement 2027: drop-in API

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/


**Yes: Microsoft deprecated Azure Content Moderator in February 2024 and retires it on March 15, 2027; its successor, Azure AI Content Safety, is a different API with different requests and results** ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-moderator/overview)). To keep code that reads `Terms`, `PII` and `Classification`, point your `ProcessText/Screen` calls at a wire-compatible endpoint such as our [Content Moderator drop-in on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/content-moderator-compat): same request, same JSON, $1 per 1,000 texts.

Microsoft's [lifecycle page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/products/azure-ai-content-moderator) lists the retirement as April 1, 2027 (06:59 PT). The product notice says March 15, 2027, so plan for **March 15**. If you prefer to move to Content Safety, see [Content Moderator vs Content Safety: what changes](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-to-content-safety/).

## What changes on March 15, 2027

- Existing Content Moderator resources stop being supported. Microsoft has deprecated the service since February 2024, so plan no new work on it.
- `POST https://<region>.api.cognitive.microsoft.com/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen` and the SDKs built on it (`Microsoft.Azure.CognitiveServices.ContentModerator`, `azure-cognitiveservices-vision-contentmoderator`) lose their service.
- Code, stored results and dashboards that depend on `Terms`, `PII`, `Classification.Category1/2/3`, `ReviewRecommended` or `Status.Code 3000` have no equivalent in Content Safety. It returns severity levels for Hate, Sexual, Violence and SelfHarm instead.

## The minimal migration: host and key only

The new endpoint is the Actor's Standby URL, `https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor`. Authenticate with your [Apify API token](https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations) as `Authorization: Bearer …` (or `?token=…`). An `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key` header is accepted and ignored. Path, query string, raw-text body and response are unchanged.

### curl

```diff
- curl -s -X POST "https://westus.api.cognitive.microsoft.com/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True" \
-   -H "Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: $AZURE_KEY" \
+ curl -s -X POST "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True" \
+   -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" \
    -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' --data-binary 'Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com?'
```

### Python (`requests`)

```diff
- BASE = "https://westus.api.cognitive.microsoft.com"
- AUTH = {"Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key": os.environ["AZURE_KEY"]}
+ BASE = "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor"
+ AUTH = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"]}
  r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen",
                    params={"language": "eng", "classify": "True", "PII": "True"},
                    headers={"Content-Type": "text/plain", **AUTH}, data=text.encode("utf-8"))
```

### Node.js (`fetch`)

```diff
- const BASE = 'https://westus.api.cognitive.microsoft.com';
- const AUTH = { 'Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key': process.env.AZURE_KEY };
+ const BASE = 'https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor';
+ const AUTH = { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.APIFY_TOKEN}` };
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE}/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True`, {
    method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain', ...AUTH }, body: text,
  });
```

## Real output on Microsoft's own example

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  --data-binary 'Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com, phone: 6657789887, IP: 255.255.255.255, 1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052'
```

Our response matches Microsoft's published `NormalizedText`, the `Terms` entry (`crap` at Index 10) and every PII index:

```json
{
  "OriginalText": "Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com, phone: 6657789887, IP: 255.255.255.255, 1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052",
  "NormalizedText": "Is this a crap email abcdef@ abcd. com, phone: 6657789887, IP: 255. 255. 255. 255, 1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052",
  "Misrepresentation": null,
  "PII": {
    "Email": [{ "Detected": "abcdef@abcd.com", "SubType": "Regular", "Text": "abcdef@abcd.com", "Index": 21 }],
    "SSN": [],
    "IPA": [{ "SubType": "IPV4", "Text": "255.255.255.255", "Index": 61 }],
    "Phone": [{ "CountryCode": "US", "Text": "6657789887", "Index": 45 }],
    "Address": [{ "Text": "1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052", "Index": 78 }]
  },
  "Classification": {
    "ReviewRecommended": true,
    "Category1": { "Score": 0.0023 },
    "Category2": { "Score": 0.2708 },
    "Category3": { "Score": 0.9562 }
  },
  "Language": "eng",
  "Terms": [{ "Index": 10, "OriginalIndex": 10, "ListId": 0, "Term": "crap" }],
  "Status": { "Code": 3000, "Description": "OK", "Exception": null },
  "TrackingId": "…"
}
```

### C# (`HttpClient`, .NET 6+)

```csharp
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using System.Text;
using System.Text.Json;

var baseUrl = "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor";
var token = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("APIFY_TOKEN")!;

using var http = new HttpClient();
http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);

var content = new StringContent("Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com?", Encoding.UTF8, "text/plain");
var response = await http.PostAsync(
    $"{baseUrl}/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True", content);
response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();

using var json = JsonDocument.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
var root = json.RootElement;
Console.WriteLine($"Status {root.GetProperty("Status").GetProperty("Code").GetInt32()}, " +
                  $"Category3 {root.GetProperty("Classification").GetProperty("Category3").GetProperty("Score").GetDouble():F3}, " +
                  $"first term '{root.GetProperty("Terms")[0].GetProperty("Term").GetString()}'");
// Status 3000, Category3 0.971, first term 'crap'
```

If you use the old `Microsoft.Azure.CognitiveServices.ContentModerator` SDK, set `client.Endpoint` to the Standby URL and pass `ServiceClientCredentials` that add the `Authorization: Bearer` header. *We tested the REST path above, not that SDK.*

## Your options compared

| Option | Same ProcessText/Screen request and JSON? | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Content Moderator drop-in on Apify (this page)** | **Yes**: change host and key | **$1 per 1,000 texts** | Terms (24-language open list), PII, Classification. Category scores approximate. No custom term lists, image or video |
| [Azure AI Content Safety](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/overview) | No: `text:analyze` returns severity levels | Free F0 tier 5,000 transactions/month; paid per Azure pricing | Microsoft's successor. Custom blocklists, 100+ languages. Needs a rewrite and re-tuned thresholds |
| [OpenAI moderation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/moderation) (`omni-moderation-latest`) | No | Free with an OpenAI account | Policy categories; no term offsets or PII |
| Self-host: [Detoxify](https://github.com/unitaryai/detoxify) + [Microsoft Presidio](https://github.com/microsoft/presidio) for PII | No: you build the API | Free (Apache-2.0 / MIT) + your servers | Most control, most work |

If you can rewrite the integration and re-tune thresholds, Content Safety is the supported path. The drop-in is for code, stored results and dashboards that depend on the old response format.

## What is identical, approximate, or unsupported

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| Route, method, query parameters (case-insensitive), `text/plain`/`html`/`xml`/`markdown` bodies, 1,024-character limit | **Identical** |
| Field names, casing and order; `Status` 3000; `Terms: null` when clean; `Misrepresentation: null`; `TrackingId` | **Identical** |
| `NormalizedText`; `Terms` `Index` and `OriginalIndex` offsets | Identical on Microsoft's documented examples. Unusual inputs may normalize differently |
| `PII` (Email, IPA, Phone, Address, SSN) | Same shape. Patterns are deliberately strict: US/UK phones, US addresses with state and ZIP |
| Built-in profanity list (`ListId 0`) | Same format. The word list is open (LDNOOBW, CC-BY-4.0, 24 languages), so matches can differ from Azure's private list |
| `Classification` Category1 (explicit), Category3 (offensive) | **Approximate.** Open Detoxify model; scores differ from Azure's |
| `Classification` Category2 (suggestive) | **Approximate proxy:** `max(Category1, 0.3 × obscene)`. Flirty but clean text is not detected |
| `ReviewRecommended` | True when any category is ≥ 0.5. Azure's own thresholds were never published |
| Classification for non-English text | Omitted, as in Azure |
| `autocorrect=true` | Accepted. The field is returned, but no spelling correction is applied |
| Custom term lists (`listId`), image/video moderation, list management, review tool | **Not supported** |

## Pricing

**$1 per 1,000 screened texts**, pay per event.
- Requests that fail validation are not charged.
- There is no subscription.
- You can cap spending per run on Apify (`429 TooManyRequests` at the cap).

## FAQ

### Is Azure Content Moderator being retired?

Yes. Microsoft deprecated it in February 2024 and retires it on March 15, 2027. Microsoft's lifecycle table lists April 1, 2027, but the product notice says March 15, 2027, so plan for March 15.

### What replaces Azure Content Moderator?

Microsoft's replacement is Azure AI Content Safety, which uses a different API: `text:analyze` with severity levels for Hate, Sexual, Violence and SelfHarm. To keep the old `ProcessText/Screen` request and JSON, use a wire-compatible endpoint such as this page's drop-in.

### How do I migrate from Azure Content Moderator without rewriting code?

Change the host from `<region>.api.cognitive.microsoft.com` to the drop-in's Standby URL and send your Apify token as `Authorization: Bearer …` instead of `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key`. The path, query parameters, body and response JSON stay the same.

### Should I just move to Content Safety?

If you can rewrite the integration and re-tune thresholds, yes, that is Microsoft's supported path. This replacement is for teams whose code, stored results and dashboards depend on the old response format.

### Are custom term lists supported?

No. The drop-in supports the built-in profanity list (`ListId 0`), PII and classification. Custom term lists, image and video moderation are not supported.

### Do you store text?

No. Nothing is written to disk or logged.

### How are short non-English texts handled?

Latin-script text under 40 characters is treated as English. Pass `language=spa`, `language=deu` and so on to use the right profanity list.

## Get started

**[Azure Content Moderator drop-in on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/content-moderator-compat)**: copy its Standby URL and your token, then change the endpoint in your code.

# Content Moderator: PII, video and review migration

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-pii-video-review-migration/


**There is no single endpoint that replaces every Azure Content Moderator feature: text compatibility, PII detection, video analysis and human review require separate migration decisions. Keep supported text-screening fields with the compatibility Actor, or move to Content Safety's different semantics, while routing broader PII to Azure Language and rebuilding video and review workflows.**

*Verified on October 4, 2026 against the linked Microsoft documentation and the Actor's current request parser, PII patterns, handler, README and pricing configuration.*

Microsoft's [Content Moderator documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-moderator/export-delete-data) gives **March 15, 2027**, while its [lifecycle table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/products/azure-ai-content-moderator) gives **April 1, 2027**. Plan for the earlier date and confirm your subscription's notice; the [main migration guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-to-content-safety/) explains the request and taxonomy changes.

## Route each feature explicitly

Here, “direct” means the supported HTTP route and field shape can remain; it does not mean identical detection results. Microsoft's [migration map](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-moderator/content-moderator) establishes the separate-service routes below.

| Existing feature | Route to evaluate | Migration class | Compatibility Actor boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text `ProcessText/Screen` | Keep the text Actor, or adopt Content Safety text analysis | Direct supported contract with Actor; different semantics on Content Safety | Raw text body and old field names; independent models and lists |
| `PII` detection | Azure AI Language PII detection for a broader entity workflow | Different service and response semantics | Limited pattern-based `Email`, `IPA`, `Phone`, `Address`, `SSN` fields |
| Custom term lists | Content Safety blocklists | Different management and matching semantics | `listId` does not load your custom lists |
| Image classification | Content Safety image analysis | Different categories and response | No image endpoint |
| Image OCR / faces | Azure AI Vision / Azure AI Face respectively | Separate services | Neither supported |
| Video moderation | Extract frames, analyze images, and screen an audio transcript | No direct video replacement | No video endpoint |
| Review API / human-review tool | Evaluate Content Safety Studio and your review application | No direct legacy API replacement established | No reviewer queue, callbacks or review storage |

## PII: preserve fields or adopt a separate entity service

The text Actor only includes `PII` when requested with `PII=True`. Its patterns cover email, IPv4/IPv6, US/UK phones, valid-format US SSNs and US street addresses with state/ZIP. They do not constitute a universal entity detector: names, passports, arbitrary national identifiers and worldwide phone/address formats are outside this contract.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X POST "https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&PII=True&classify=True" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: text/plain" \
  --data-binary 'Please reply to support@example.com.'
```

The body limit is **1,024 JavaScript string code units**; the parser uses `text.length`, so a supplementary character such as an emoji consumes two. Supported content types are `text/plain`, `text/html`, `text/xml` and `text/markdown`. Apify authenticates the Bearer token; an old `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key` header is ignored.

Azure Language's [PII feature](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/language-service/personally-identifiable-information/overview) provides entity recognition and redaction capabilities. For migration, map its results to your application deliberately: validate entity categories, language coverage, offsets and redacted output on your own samples. An empty match list from either service is evidence about that detector's coverage, not proof a document contains no personal information.

## Video: build and verify a pipeline

Microsoft recommends sampling frames for image analysis and analyzing an audio transcription separately. Its guide does not offer a direct replacement for the old video API. [Microsoft video migration guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-moderator/content-moderator)

A practical migration needs to retain the source time for each frame and transcript segment, combine those results under your own policy, and route uncertain segments for review. Test a short harmful scene between sampled frames and a harmful audio passage without an accompanying image: coarse frame sampling can miss either case.

The [public-media URL transcription guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/public-media-url-to-srt-vtt/) can supply segment-timed text from a direct media file. Transcription itself is not video moderation, and the text compatibility Actor does not extract frames or combine decisions.

## Human review: a flag is not a review system

Microsoft maps the old Review API to Content Safety Studio as web-based monitoring. Its [Studio overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/overview) describes testing, moderation workflows and monitoring; that does not establish drop-in support for your old review IDs, reviewer assignments or callbacks.

Inventory those dependencies before switching. Demonstrate how an item enters a queue, who can decide, how a callback or polling client learns the outcome, and how you retain the decision history. Validate these behaviors in the chosen system rather than treating a dashboard as evidence of API compatibility.

The text Actor's `Classification.ReviewRecommended` is just a boolean: for English classification it becomes true when any approximate Category1/2/3 score reaches 0.5. Category2 is a proxy, `max(Category1, 0.3 × obscene)`, and misses flirty but otherwise clean text. Non-English classification is omitted. The Actor never assigns a reviewer or persists a review decision.

## Custom policies and validation

`listId` requests continue with the built-in list; a nonzero custom ID gets an `X-Compat-Warning` header. Custom lists are not migrated. `autocorrect=True` returns `AutoCorrectedText` equal to normalized text, with no spelling correction. Check those headers and behaviors before relying on old policy settings.

Run known positive and negative samples for every retained feature. Separate detector quality from workflow quality: a correct PII match does not prove redaction happened, and a recommended review does not prove a reviewer received the item. [DoneLatch evidence checks](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-coding-agent-done-without-evidence/) can record your tests after an agent's final edit.

For supported text screening, the price is **$0.001 per `text-screened` event ($1 per 1,000)** plus Apify's run-start charge. Validation failures have no text event. At the configured spending cap, the handler returns `429` with `Error.Code: TooManyRequests`.

**[Try the text-compatible Content Moderator Actor](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/content-moderator-compat)** when your requirement is the bounded text contract above.

## FAQ

### Is Azure AI Content Safety a PII replacement?

Its text harm-analysis endpoint does not replace PII detection. Microsoft routes PII to Azure AI Language. The compatibility Actor keeps limited pattern-based PII fields for supported text requests.

### Can I send a video to the compatibility Actor?

No. It only screens text. Microsoft's migration route requires a separate frame/image and audio/transcript pipeline, with your own time mapping and policy decisions.

### Does ReviewRecommended create a human-review task?

No. It is a classification flag. A review queue, reviewer permissions, notifications, decisions and history require a separate workflow.

### Will my Azure custom term list still run?

No. The Actor uses its built-in list, and a nonzero listId returns a compatibility-warning header. Export and migrate your list into the replacement system separately.

## Related

- Parent: [Content Moderator to Content Safety: what changes](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-to-content-safety/).
- Adjacent: [Perspective attributeScores migration](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-attributescores-migration/).
- Product details: [Content Moderator text alternative](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/).

# Content Moderator to Content Safety: what changes

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-to-content-safety/


**Microsoft points Content Moderator customers to Azure AI Content Safety, but it is not a new version of the same API. It uses a different endpoint (`text:analyze`), a different JSON body and a different taxonomy (Hate, Sexual, Violence and SelfHarm severities). PII, video and human review each move to a different Microsoft product, so every workflow needs its own migration decision** ([Microsoft migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-moderator/content-moderator)).

*Facts on this page were checked against the linked Microsoft Learn pages on October 3, 2026.*

**Which date?** Microsoft gives two retirement dates:
- Content Moderator's documentation says it "will be retired on March 15, 2027" ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-moderator/export-delete-data)).
- The lifecycle table lists April 1, 2027, 06:59 Pacific time ([lifecycle](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/products/azure-ai-content-moderator)).

Plan for the earlier date, and check the retirement notice for your own subscription.

If you would rather not rewrite the text-screening call before then, a [wire-compatible Content Moderator replacement](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/) keeps `ProcessText/Screen` working with only a host and key change.

## Where each Content Moderator feature goes

| Content Moderator feature | Microsoft's replacement | Like for like? |
|---|---|---|
| Text classification (Category1/2/3, `ReviewRecommended`) | Content Safety `text:analyze` (Hate, Sexual, Violence, SelfHarm) | No. New taxonomy and scale; re-tune thresholds. |
| Profanity terms and custom term lists | Content Safety blocklists (up to 10,000 terms per list, regex support) | Partly. No built-in profanity list with offsets. |
| PII in text | Azure AI Language PII detection | No. A separate service and API. |
| Image moderation | Content Safety image analysis | No. Different categories and response. |
| OCR on images | Azure AI Vision | No. A separate service. |
| Face detection | Azure AI Face | No. A separate service. |
| Video moderation | None. The guide says to extract frames and use the image API. | No direct equivalent |
| Review API and human review tool | Content Safety Studio (web-based monitoring) | No. A different workflow. |

Source: [Microsoft's migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-moderator/content-moderator). The free F0 tier of Content Safety includes 5,000 transactions a month.

## The two requests side by side

**Content Moderator (retiring):**

```bash
curl -X POST "https://<region>.api.cognitive.microsoft.com/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True&PII=True" \
  -H "Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: text/plain" \
  --data-binary 'Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com?'
```

**Content Safety (Microsoft's replacement),** per Microsoft's [text quickstart](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/quickstart-text):

```bash
curl -X POST "<endpoint>/contentsafety/text:analyze?api-version=2024-09-01" \
  -H "Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "Is this a crap email abcdef@abcd.com?", "categories": ["Hate", "Sexual", "SelfHarm", "Violence"], "outputType": "FourSeverityLevels"}'
```

Content Safety returns `categoriesAnalysis` (for example `{"category": "Hate", "severity": 2}`) and `blocklistsMatch`. Text severities are `0, 2, 4, 6` (four levels) or the full `0–7` scale (eight levels) ([harm categories](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/concepts/harm-categories)).

## Field-by-field mapping

| Content Moderator `ProcessText/Screen` | Content Safety `text:analyze` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Raw text body (`text/plain`, `html`, `xml`, `markdown`) | JSON `{"text": "..."}` | Body format changes |
| Query `language`, `classify`, `PII`, `autocorrect`, `listId` | JSON `categories`, `blocklistNames`, `haltOnBlocklistHit`, `outputType` | Different parameters |
| `Terms[]` (built-in profanity list, `ListId 0`, with `Index`/`OriginalIndex`) | `blocklistsMatch[]` from **your own** blocklists | No built-in profanity list with offsets |
| `PII` (Email, IPA, Phone, Address, SSN with indexes) | None | Use a separate PII service, such as Azure AI Language PII detection |
| `Classification.Category1` (explicit), `Category2` (suggestive), `Category3` (offensive), each 0–1 | `Sexual`, `Hate`, `Violence`, `SelfHarm` severity levels | No 1:1 mapping; re-tune thresholds |
| `Classification.ReviewRecommended` | None | Derive from your own severity thresholds |
| `NormalizedText`, `AutoCorrectedText`, `Misrepresentation` | None | |
| `Status.Code 3000`, `TrackingId` | HTTP status and error body | Error handling changes |
| Image moderation | Image analysis (separate endpoint) | Video has no direct equivalent |

## Which way to go

| Situation | Path |
|---|---|
| You can rewrite the call and re-tune thresholds before March 2027 | Move to Content Safety (Microsoft's supported path; free F0 tier of 5,000 transactions a month) |
| Your code, stored results or dashboards depend on `Terms`, `PII` or `Category1/2/3` | Keep the format with a [wire-compatible replacement](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/) ($1 per 1,000 texts) and migrate later on your own schedule |
| You use PII detection, video, OCR, faces or the review tool | The Microsoft service in the table above; the wire-compatible replacement covers **text** screening only |
| You only need a free generic moderation signal | OpenAI's `omni-moderation-latest` (free), also with a different API |

The minimal change with the wire-compatible replacement:

```diff
- POST https://<region>.api.cognitive.microsoft.com/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True
- Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: $AZURE_KEY
+ POST https://dropin-apis--content-moderator-compat.apify.actor/contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen?language=eng&classify=True
+ Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN
```

## FAQ

### Is Azure Content Safety the same API as Content Moderator?

No. Content Safety uses `POST /contentsafety/text:analyze` with a JSON body and returns severity levels for Hate, Sexual, Violence and SelfHarm. Content Moderator's `ProcessText/Screen` took a raw text body and returned `Terms`, `PII` and `Classification` scores.

### Does Content Safety detect PII like Content Moderator did?

Not in `text:analyze`. Microsoft's guide moves PII detection to Azure AI Language. A wire-compatible replacement can keep the old `PII` field (email, IP, US/UK phone, US SSN, US address).

### How do Content Moderator categories map to Content Safety?

Roughly: Category1 (sexually explicit) and Category2 (suggestive) relate to Sexual, and Category3 (offensive) overlaps with Hate and Violence. The scales differ (0–1 scores versus severity levels), so thresholds must be re-tuned on your own data.

### When does Azure Content Moderator stop working?

Microsoft's Content Moderator documentation says March 15, 2027, while its lifecycle table lists April 1, 2027. Plan for March 15 and check the notice for your subscription.

### Can I keep using ProcessText/Screen after the retirement?

Not on Azure. A wire-compatible replacement accepts the same `ProcessText/Screen` request and returns the same JSON from a new host.

### What replaces Content Moderator video moderation and the review tool?

Video has no direct replacement. Microsoft suggests extracting frames and sending them to the image API. The Review API and human review tool move to Content Safety Studio, which is a different workflow.

## Related

- Up: [all retiring-API guides](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/)
- Next: [Perspective API shutdown checklist](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-shutdown-checklist/)
- **[Keep ProcessText/Screen on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/content-moderator-compat)** ($1 per 1,000 texts, text screening only)

# Does This Function Exist in This Package Version?

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/check-function-exists-package-version/


**Check the package name, exact version and symbol together before an agent writes the call: a real package can still lack that function in the version your lockfile selected. ExactGround reads the published npm or PyPI artifact without installing or executing it and returns `exists: true`, `false`, or `null` when static evidence cannot decide.**

*Facts and examples on this page were checked against the ExactGround API source, tests, README and linked package-format documentation on October 4, 2026.*

## The exact-version question

“Does this package exist?” and “does this function exist here?” are different checks. A package can be real while an agent uses an API added in a later release, removed in the pinned release, hidden behind an npm export boundary, or supplied dynamically at runtime.

Use the version resolved by your lockfile, not the newest documentation page. npm package specifications can be exact versions, ranges or dist-tags ([npm package spec](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/using-npm/package-spec/)), while Node's `exports` field can expose only selected entry points and hide other package files ([Node.js package entry points](https://nodejs.org/api/packages.html#package-entry-points)). PyPI's JSON API identifies the release artifacts available for a project and version ([PyPI JSON API](https://docs.pypi.org/api/json/)).

## One request, one answer per symbol

```bash
curl -s https://dropin-apis--exactground-api.apify.actor/v1/symbols \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ecosystem":"pypi","package":"numpy","version":"2.1.0","symbols":["numpy.linalg.norm","numpy.asfarray"]}'
```

The verified example returns:

```json
{
  "ecosystem": "pypi",
  "package": "numpy",
  "version": "2.1.0",
  "packageExists": true,
  "results": [
    {
      "symbol": "numpy.linalg.norm",
      "exists": true,
      "kind": "function",
      "declaredIn": "numpy/linalg/_linalg.pyi"
    },
    {
      "symbol": "numpy.asfarray",
      "exists": false,
      "missingAt": "numpy.asfarray",
      "suggestions": ["array", "asarray", "NDArray", "ndarray", "recarray"]
    }
  ]
}
```

For npm, the tested React example reports `react@18.2.0` `useState` as present and `useActionState` as absent. Its response identifies `@types/react@18.3.31 (DefinitelyTyped)` as the matching-major type source; that is evidence from the declaration fallback, not a claim that runtime implementation bytes were executed.

## Interpret `true`, `false` and `null` differently

| Result | Meaning | Safe next action |
|---|---|---|
| `true` | The resolved artifact's static public surface contains the symbol | Continue, then run your own tests |
| `false` | The static surface establishes that the requested path is missing | Correct the call or version before editing |
| `null` | Static analysis cannot know | Inspect runtime docs/source or test in an isolated environment; do not turn unknown into yes |

`null` is expected for cases such as a Python module with dynamic `__getattr__`, a compiled extension, or an npm package with no types. ExactGround does not guess in those cases.

## What the checker reads

- **npm:** resolves the requested exact version, range or dist-tag, reads the tarball in memory, follows `exports`, `types` and `typesVersions`, and uses the TypeScript resolver. A package without bundled types can use a matching-major `@types/*` fallback, disclosed in `typesSource`.
- **PyPI:** reads a suitable wheel or source distribution in memory, prefers `.pyi` stubs, and statically follows ordinary re-exports, `__all__`, class members and base classes.
- **Neither ecosystem is executed:** no install scripts and no Python imports. Archives are capped at 60 MB. Private registries are not supported by this hosted API.

Static package inspection answers availability, not safety, behavior or compatibility with the rest of your application. A present symbol can still be buggy, insecure, or misused.

## Put it in an agent's decision loop

1. Read the locked package and version from the project's lockfile.
2. Call `check_packages` before any new install; a published name is not automatically trustworthy.
3. Call `check_symbols` for an uncertain function, class or method before writing the call.
4. Treat `false` as a block and `null` as an unresolved review item.
5. After editing, run project tests and require fresh completion evidence.

The MCP tool is `check_symbols`; the REST endpoint is `POST /v1/symbols`. Each symbol check costs **$0.002**. Invalid input and registry-unreachable requests are not charged, and a configured spending limit stops with HTTP 402 when reached.

## FAQ

### Can it check a function against the version in package-lock.json or poetry.lock?

Yes, after the agent or caller supplies the resolved package name and exact version from that lockfile. The endpoint does not read your local lockfile by itself.

### Does `exists: true` prove the function works?

No. It proves the static published surface contains the symbol. You still need behavioral tests, compatibility checks and security review.

### Why can `exists` be `null`?

Some APIs are created dynamically, implemented only in compiled code, or published without analyzable declarations. Returning unknown is more accurate than reporting a guessed yes or no.

### Does the API install or import the package?

No. It reads bounded public package archives in memory and parses their static surface.

- Up: [check whether an npm or PyPI package exists](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/check-npm-package-exists-api/)
- Before install: [stop agents installing hallucinated packages](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-agent-hallucinated-packages/)
- After editing: [make agent completion require evidence](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-coding-agent-done-without-evidence/)
- **[Open ExactGround API on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/exactground-api)** · [free local install guard](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground)

# Check if an npm or PyPI Package Exists — API & MCP

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/check-npm-package-exists-api/


**This API answers one question an AI coding agent can't answer on its own: does this npm or PyPI package exist, and does the function or method it's about to call actually exist in the exact version pinned in your lockfile?** It reads the published package itself — TypeScript `.d.ts` declarations, DefinitelyTyped, Python wheel source and `.pyi` stubs — without running any of its code, and answers over MCP or REST.

## Why this exists

A USENIX Security 2025 study (Spracklen et al.) had 16 models write **576,000 code samples**. Of the **2.23 million package recommendations** in them, **440,445 (19.7%) named packages that do not exist**, 205,474 unique names. In a separate test, the authors re-ran 500 prompts that had produced a hallucination 10 times each, and 43% of those hallucinated names came back in all 10 runs ([paper](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity25/presentation/spracklen)). Predictable names are what make "slopsquatting" (registering the invented name with malware) practical.

The quieter failure is calling a real API that isn't in *your* version — `useActionState` exists in React 19 but not React 18; `numpy.asfarray` was removed in NumPy 2.0. The code looks right, passes review, and breaks at runtime.

## What it checks

| Endpoint | Question it answers | Price |
|---|---|---|
| `check_symbols` / `POST /v1/symbols` | Does `symbol` exist in `package@version`? Returns `exists`, kind, signature, deprecation notes and did-you-mean suggestions | $0.002 per symbol |
| `check_packages` / `POST /v1/packages` | Does the package exist? Was the pinned version published? Is it a look-alike of a popular package, brand new, or an npm security placeholder? | $0.0005 per package |
| `check_diff` / `POST /v1/diff` | For a diff: every added import, and whether each imported name exists in the pinned version | $0.01 per diff |

`exists: null` means "cannot be known statically" (a dynamic Python `__getattr__`, a compiled extension, or an untyped npm package) — it is never reported as a guess.

## Example (real output)

```bash
curl -s https://dropin-apis--exactground-api.apify.actor/v1/symbols \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ecosystem":"pypi","package":"numpy","version":"2.1.0","symbols":["numpy.linalg.norm","numpy.asfarray"]}'
```

```json
{
  "ecosystem": "pypi", "package": "numpy", "version": "2.1.0", "packageExists": true,
  "results": [
    { "symbol": "numpy.linalg.norm", "exists": true, "kind": "function" },
    { "symbol": "numpy.asfarray", "exists": false, "missingAt": "numpy.asfarray",
      "suggestions": ["array", "asarray", "NDArray", "ndarray", "recarray"] }
  ]
}
```

A package check on a typo'd name:

```json
{ "ecosystem": "pypi", "name": "reqeusts", "verdict": "block", "registry": "missing",
  "reasons": ["\"reqeusts\" does not exist on PyPI", "did you mean \"requests\"? (it is 1 edit away)"] }
```

## How it compares

| Tool | Answers | What it's for |
|---|---|---|
| **This Actor** | Yes/no, from the published artifact itself | Does this exact name/version/symbol exist |
| Context7 | Documentation text for a prompt | What does this library's docs say |
| Socket | Security score for packages that exist | Is this existing package malicious or risky |

Context7 and Socket solve different, adjacent problems — this tool is the one that catches a name or API that was never real in the first place.

## Connect an agent (MCP)

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http exactground https://dropin-apis--exactground-api.apify.actor/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN"
```

Also works with Cursor, VS Code, Codex and any MCP-compatible client (`mcp.json` or `~/.codex/config.toml`), and can be found by agents on the [Apify MCP server](https://mcp.apify.com) via `search-actors`.

## Pricing

Pay per event, no subscription. A typical agent session (5 package checks, 20 symbol checks, 2 diffs) costs about **$0.06**. Requests that fail (invalid input, registry unreachable) are not charged; setting a maximum total charge stops the API with HTTP 402 once reached.

**[Open ExactGround on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/exactground-api)** · [Free local install guard](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground)

## FAQ

### How do I stop Claude Code or Cursor from installing hallucinated packages?

Install the free [ExactGround hook](https://github.com/alidaram99/exactground) — it blocks `npm`/`pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun`/`npx` and `pip`/`uv`/`poetry`/`pdm`/`pipx` installs of names that don't exist, before they run. This API adds version-exact function/method checks on top.

### What is slopsquatting?

Attackers publish malware under package names AI models tend to invent. When an agent runs an install command on the invented name, it installs the attacker's code instead.

### How is this different from Context7?

Context7 puts documentation text into the prompt. This API answers a yes/no question from the published artifact itself — does a given symbol exist in a given version — and returns a verdict (`ok`, `warn` or `block`). It does not intercept installs itself; the free local ExactGround hook is what refuses an install in your agent.

### Which languages are supported?

npm (JavaScript and TypeScript) and PyPI (Python).

### Is my code sent anywhere?

Only what you send in a request — package names and symbol paths, or a diff for `check_diff`. Nothing is stored after the response.

### Is this affiliated with npm, PyPI, Anthropic, OpenAI or Cursor?

No. It is an independent tool.

# Get Competitor App Store Reviews, No Connect Key

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/competitor-app-store-reviews-no-connect-key/


**Apple's App Store Connect API is built for apps your own team owns** — authenticating into it to read a competitor's reviews isn't an option, because Apple's Customer Reviews endpoint only serves reviews for apps linked to your own developer account. **This Actor instead reads Apple's public, unauthenticated customer-review feed** (JSON, with an automatic XML fallback), which works for any app on the App Store, yours or a competitor's, with no login, no Connect key, and no CAPTCHA bypass.

## Why App Store Connect doesn't work for this

Apple's own [Customer Reviews documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appstoreconnectapi/customer-reviews) frames the endpoint around an app the authenticated developer account owns — there's no parameter that lets you query someone else's app by id. That's a deliberate scope limit, not a bug to route around: this Actor doesn't attempt to defeat it. It uses a separate, genuinely public surface — the same review feed the App Store's own web and app clients read from — which Apple exposes without authentication for every published app.

## What you get

One row per review (`rating` 1–5, `title`, `text`, `version`, `date`, helpfulness `voteCount`/`voteSum`), plus an optional app-details row per app × country with name, developer, price, average rating and rating count. Real review row:

```json
{
  "type": "review",
  "appId": "570060128",
  "appName": "Duolingo: Language Lessons",
  "country": "us",
  "reviewId": "14612250135",
  "title": "Fun",
  "text": "Very fun and get one month free for unlimited power",
  "rating": 5,
  "version": "7.142.0",
  "date": "2026-09-30T13:01:34-07:00",
  "voteCount": 0,
  "voteSum": 0,
  "developerResponse": null,
  "source": "rss-json"
}
```

## Run it

```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/dropin-apis~app-store-reviews/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"apps":["<competitor app id or apps.apple.com URL>"],"countries":["us","gb"],"maxReviewsPerApp":200}'
```

Pass a numeric app id or a full `apps.apple.com` URL — both work. Add every country storefront you care about: reviews, ratings and even pricing genuinely differ by storefront (see the companion page on why totals differ by country, linked below).

## Honest boundary

This is public-feed data, not every review that has ever existed for an app. `developerResponse` is always `null` — developer replies aren't part of Apple's public feed at all, so there's no reply text to scrape for a competitor or for yourself. Apple's feed is occasionally empty for a run; the Actor retries and falls back from JSON to XML before giving up, and only adds a `type:"warning"` row (never a silent empty success) if both stay empty for an app known to have ratings.

## Limits

Up to **500 reviews per app per country** — Apple's own public feed stops at 10 pages of 50, not an Actor-side cap. Query more countries for more coverage, since each storefront has its own review pool. No developer-response text. Review language follows the storefront's dominant language.

## Pricing

Pay per event — **$0.0002 per row** ($0.20 per 1,000), review rows and app-details rows both counted, no subscription.

**[Open App Store Reviews Scraper on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)**

## FAQ

### Can I get a competitor's App Store reviews without their cooperation?

Yes, for public reviews. App Store Connect needs the app owner's own account; this Actor instead reads Apple's public customer-review feed, which is readable for any published app without authentication. It does not access anything private, unpublished, or owner-only (like developer-reply text, which isn't in the public feed for any app, including your own).

### Do I need an Apple developer account at all?

No developer account, Connect key, or Apple login of any kind. You need an [Apify account](https://apify.com) and token to run the Actor.

### Why would two runs of the same app return slightly different review counts?

New reviews post continuously, and Apple's own feed pagination can shift slightly between requests. Treat a run as a snapshot at that time, not an immutable historical record — rerun on a schedule if you're tracking trends.

### Is this allowed under Apple's terms?

The Actor only reads Apple's own public, unauthenticated endpoints — the same ones the App Store's web and app clients use — and does not bypass any login, CAPTCHA, or rate limit designed to block it. It does not use Apple's authenticated web API (which needs a session token and returns HTTP 401 without one). Review your own use against Apple's terms for your specific case; this page isn't legal advice.

### What's the difference between this page and the main App Store Reviews Scraper page?

That page covers the full Actor: inputs, output shapes, pricing, and the general use cases. This page answers the specific question of collecting a **competitor's** reviews without owning their Connect account — see also [why review counts differ by country](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/app-store-reviews-differ-by-country/) if your counts look incomplete.

# Extract All URLs From a Sitemap — indexes, gzip, robots.txt

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/extract-urls-from-sitemap/


**Give this Actor a domain or sitemap URL, and it returns one row per page URL from the site's public sitemap** — it does not open or crawl those pages, only the sitemap files themselves. It follows sitemap indexes, unpacks `.xml.gz`, and checks `robots.txt` for `Sitemap:` lines.

## What it looks up

Given a domain, it checks (in order): `robots.txt` (every `Sitemap:` line), then `/sitemap.xml` and `/sitemap_index.xml` if not already listed. A start URL that already ends in `.xml` or `.xml.gz` is fetched directly. An index is followed one child file at a time until `maxUrls` is reached; a file starting with the gzip magic bytes is unpacked automatically.

## Example input

```json
{
  "startUrls": [{ "url": "https://www.sitemaps.org" }],
  "maxUrls": 10
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `startUrls` | required | A domain or a sitemap URL (`.xml` or `.xml.gz`) |
| `includeRegex` / `excludeRegex` | optional | Case-insensitive regex to keep or drop matching URLs |
| `lastmodSince` | optional | ISO date — URLs with an older `lastmod` are dropped; URLs with no `lastmod` are kept |
| `maxUrls` | integer, default 1000 | Stop after this many unique URLs |

## Example output

```json
{
  "url": "https://www.sitemaps.org/",
  "lastmod": "2016-11-21",
  "changefreq": null,
  "priority": null,
  "sourceSitemap": "https://www.sitemaps.org/sitemap.xml",
  "domain": "www.sitemaps.org"
}
```

Both a real sitemap index (`https://apify.com`) and a gzip child sitemap (`https://www.gnu.org`'s `sitemap0.xml.gz`) were checked against live sites during development.

## Use cases

- **A URL list for another Actor or crawler** that only needs the links, not a fresh crawl of the whole site.
- **Change detection** — keep rows whose `lastmod` is after a date you pass in.
- **A scoped export** — keep or drop URLs with a regular expression (`/blog/`, a locale, a file type).

## Limits

Public `http`/`https` sitemaps only, no login; private hosts are refused. At most 50 sitemap files per run and 20 MB per file after unpacking. At most 5 fetches in flight, with retries on HTTP 429/5xx, and `Crawl-delay` in robots.txt honored up to 5 seconds. A path disallowed for `User-agent: *` is not fetched. The run **fails** if every input produces zero URLs, so an empty success is never silently reported as a finished dataset.

## Run it from code

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/dropin-apis~sitemap-url-extractor/run-sync-get-dataset-items" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"startUrls":[{"url":"https://www.sitemaps.org"}],"maxUrls":10}'
```

## Pricing

Pay per event — the primary event is `apify-default-dataset-item` at **$0.0004 per URL ($0.40 per 1,000)**, charged when a row is saved. No monthly fee.

**[Open Sitemap URL Extractor & Scraper on Apify](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/sitemap-url-extractor)**

## FAQ

### Does this crawl the pages listed in the sitemap?

No. It only downloads sitemap files and returns the URLs listed inside them — it never fetches the pages those URLs point to.

### What if the site publishes a sitemap index or a `.gz` file?

A sitemap index is followed one child file at a time until `maxUrls` is reached. A file that starts with the gzip magic bytes is unpacked automatically — both paths were checked against real live sites, not only synthetic fixtures.

### What does a plain domain input actually fetch?

`/robots.txt` first (reading every `Sitemap:` line), then `/sitemap.xml` and `/sitemap_index.xml` if those weren't already listed there. A start URL ending in `.xml` or `.xml.gz` is fetched directly, skipping the robots.txt step.

### Why did the run fail with "0 URL(s)"?

None of the inputs had a readable public sitemap. A missing `/sitemap_index.xml` on its own is normal and not a failure — the failure only triggers when every candidate sitemap was missing or wasn't valid sitemap XML.

### What does it cost?

$0.0004 per extracted URL ($0.40 per 1,000 rows), pay per event, with no subscription.

# Drop-in replacements for retiring APIs, plus data tools

URL: https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/


Three widely used APIs are being switched off between December 2026 and March 2027. Their official successors use **different requests and responses**, so every integration has to be rewritten. The tools below accept **the same request and return the same response shape** as the API you already call. You change the host, add an Apify token, and keep your code.

They run on [Apify](https://apify.com) and are billed per use, with no subscription. Each one says clearly what is identical, what is approximate and what is not supported.

## Drop-in replacements

### Google Perspective API (ends after 31 Dec 2026)
`POST /v1alpha1/comments:analyze`, with TOXICITY, INSULT, THREAT, PROFANITY, IDENTITY_ATTACK, SEXUALLY_EXPLICIT and SEVERE_TOXICITY, in 7 languages. Google's own Python client works with only the discovery URL changed. Scores come from open models: close to Perspective's, not identical.
**$1 per 1,000 comments** · [Migration guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-alternative/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/perspective-compat) · [Shutdown checklist](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/perspective-api-shutdown-checklist/)

### Azure Content Moderator, text screen (retires 15 Mar 2027)
`POST /contentmoderator/moderate/v1.0/ProcessText/Screen`, with the same `Terms`, `PII`, `Classification` and `Status` JSON. It matches Microsoft's own documented example field for field. Category scores are approximate, and custom term lists are not supported.
**$1 per 1,000 texts** · [Migration guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-alternative/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/content-moderator-compat) · [Content Moderator vs Content Safety](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/azure-content-moderator-to-content-safety/)

### OpenAI whisper-1 (removed 26 Feb 2027)
`/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/translations`, with SRT, VTT, and word and segment timestamps. It works with the official OpenAI Python and Node SDKs by changing `base_url` and `api_key`. It uses the smaller open Whisper model (about 4% word error on clear English), with up to 10 minutes per file.
**$0.006 per minute** · [Migration guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/whisper-1-alternative/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/whisper-compat) · [All OpenAI transcription models removed Feb 26, 2027](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/openai-transcription-models-deprecation-2027/)

## Data tools

### App Store reviews
Reviews and app details for any app in any country, from Apple's public feed, with no App Store Connect key. Up to 500 reviews per app per country.
**$0.20 per 1,000 rows** · [Guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/app-store-reviews-scraper/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/app-store-reviews)

### Woolworths Australia prices
Shelf price, specials and unit price per kg or litre, by search term, from public catalog data.
**$1 per 1,000 products** · [Guide](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/woolworths-api/) · [Apify Store](https://apify.com/dropin-apis/woolworths-au-products)

## Tools for AI coding agents

Free, open-source guardrails for coding agents, with answers to the questions they raise:

- [Stop agents installing packages that do not exist](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-agent-hallucinated-packages/) (ExactGround)
- [Stop agents claiming "done" without evidence](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/ai-coding-agent-done-without-evidence/) (DoneLatch)
- [Which MCP server actually works today?](https://alidaram99.github.io/api-alternatives/mcp-server-reliability/) (CanaryIndex)

## How it works

1. Create a free Apify account and copy your API token.
2. Open the tool on the Apify Store. For the API replacements, copy its **Standby URL**.
3. Point your existing code at that URL and send the token. Pay only for what you use, and set a spending cap if you like.

Nothing you send is stored: comments, texts and audio are processed in memory and discarded.
